paths.description: Homepage and primary accommodation-search entry point; represents global chrome, promotions, and search forms.
Hokkaido accommodation region page; represents destination listings and deal cards.
Activity booking landing page; represents a newer responsive booking/search template.
Travel guide index; represents editorial discovery content.
Login screen; represents authentication and account input handling.
Keyword search results/empty state; represents the primary accommodation search continuation.
Nonexistent route; represents HTTP and navigation recovery.

findings.summary: The site does not honor the user’s dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains the same white/orange fixed palette, and the computed root colorScheme is normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven surface, text, border, and image treatments.

findings.summary: Core accommodation, destination, editorial, login, and result templates render as scaled desktop canvases on mobile.
findings.evidence: At a 360px viewport the homepage uses an effective 1146px layout; Hokkaido, travel, login, and results are visibly miniaturized. Only the activity template is meaningfully responsive.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace fixed 1000/1146px shells with intrinsic grids, flexible sizing, and narrow-layout composition.

findings.summary: Shared components are not container responsive.
findings.evidence: The page probe found zero container rules, while the same global chrome and card/search modules are reused inside fixed-width shells.
findings.suggestedFix: Add container-type to reusable regions and use size-aware @container rules with intrinsic fallbacks.

findings.summary: Many controls are too small for touch even though keyboard outlines remain visible.
findings.evidence: The focus probe measured many primary links at 11 to 30px high, and Lighthouse target-size failed.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive target boxes to at least 24 CSS px, preferably 44px for primary touch actions, without shrinking visible focus.

findings.summary: State and route changes use abrupt legacy navigation.
findings.evidence: The page probe found no view-transition rules, and representative navigation is conventional full-document switching without continuity.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for same-origin archetype changes, with reduced-motion-safe fallbacks.

findings.summary: Long pages provide little responsive navigation guidance.
findings.evidence: Home and travel screenshots show long, dense pages with static chrome; probes found no container or transition treatment to reflect scroll state or guide in-page jumps.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact scroll-aware header or progress/section cue and preserve clear attention after anchor navigation.

findings.summary: Promotional chrome and advertisements overwhelm the core booking task.
findings.evidence: The homepage mobile capture is dominated by tiny banners, side rails, coupons, and repeated campaign tiles around the search form.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer nonessential campaigns, cap promotional slots, and prioritize one clear search task in the first viewport.

findings.summary: Load performance is far outside good ranges.
findings.evidence: Trace measured FCP 7.18s, LCP 7.70s and 532ms TBT; Lighthouse under mobile throttling measured LCP 60.2s, CLS 0.184, and 3,350ms TBT with a performance score of 0.17.
findings.suggestedFix: Set explicit performance budgets, prioritize the LCP resource, and remove or defer noncritical script and ad work.

findings.summary: The network dependency surface is excessive.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 481 requests and 5.84MB transferred, including 154 scripts; 276 third-party requests transferred 4.56MB and ten parser-inserted stylesheets were flagged as render-blocking candidates.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, defer noncritical scripts, gate tags on need/consent, and cache/compress reusable resources.

findings.summary: Large amounts of shipped JavaScript are unused.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 2,649 KiB of unused JavaScript and 37 KiB of unused CSS; HAR attributes 4.36MB to scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate tag destinations, split code by task, and load third-party modules only after user intent.

findings.summary: Images and form controls lack accessible alternatives and labels.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 55 of 100 images missing alt; Lighthouse failed image-alt and identified unlabeled date/person controls, while activity/login probes found 12 and 3 unlabeled controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Add meaningful alt or empty alt for decoration, and associate every input with a visible label or accessible name.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported multiple failures, including 3.35:1 placeholder text and 3.27:1 date text where 4.5:1 is required.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust text/control tokens to meet WCAG contrast in every state and preserve forced-color behavior.

findings.summary: Document structure and control semantics are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The homepage contains many empty H2 elements, Lighthouse found a skipped heading level and unnamed links, and several controls are JavaScript anchors.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic buttons for actions, remove empty headings, keep levels sequential, and name all links.

findings.summary: Zoom/reflow and target sizing are not robust across major templates.
findings.evidence: Fixed 1000 to 1146px shells are scaled into 360px viewports, login lacks viewport metadata, and Lighthouse target-size failed.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt responsive reflow, retain user scaling, and enlarge targets across legacy templates.

findings.summary: The homepage emits runtime errors and inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed errors-in-console with nine captured items and reported an inspector issue plus invalid source maps.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix uncaught/network console failures, remove deprecated integrations, and publish valid source maps for owned production bundles.

findings.summary: Asset markup is dated and destabilizing.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 23 images without dimensions, 30 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 38 without srcset, and 82 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions and responsive sources, lazy-load below-fold media, and migrate raster assets to modern formats where appropriate.

findings.summary: Some links are JavaScript actions rather than crawlable navigation and mobile friendliness is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors on javascript:void links, while several public templates are fixed-width on mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for actions, real hrefs for navigation, and responsive viewport behavior on every public template.

findings.summary: Entity metadata coverage is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The homepage has Open Graph metadata but zero JSON-LD blocks; the activity page also has zero, despite organization, destination, and product-like content.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org Organization/WebSite and relevant product/place/activity data that matches visible content.

findings.summary: Transport defenses and cookie attributes are unsafe.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are absent. Of 42 cookies, 41 lacked Secure; session-like cookies were not HttpOnly and used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP and defensive headers, then mark all HTTPS cookies Secure with appropriate SameSite and HttpOnly for session credentials.

findings.summary: The default page load has an extreme tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe saw 56 third-party origins and 12 known tracker domains; HAR recorded 276 third-party requests and 4.56MB, including Google, TikTok, Facebook, DoubleClick, Criteo, Bing, and others.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize tags, require contextual consent where needed, batch analytics, and load only vendors tied to demonstrated user value.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only and disables browser credential assistance.
findings.evidence: The login probe found no WebAuthn/passkey code; username and password both set autocomplete=off and lack associated labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey sign-in and use username/current-password autocomplete as a fallback.

findings.summary: Important metadata and content are only partially preserved without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Crawler comparisons found 50% content overlap on activity and 64% on Hokkaido; raw responses did not preserve rendered title or H1 on sampled pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render stable title, H1, core search/listing content, and functional form actions before enhancing with JavaScript.

findings.summary: The booking experience has no install or offline fallback surface.
findings.evidence: Representative probes found no manifest URL and no controlling service worker; the site is a repeat-use commerce service with extensive search forms.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a manifest and a conservative offline/error fallback for previously visited and interrupted journeys.

findings.summary: Language metadata is missing on important Japanese pages.
findings.evidence: The Hokkaido region and login probes returned an empty html lang, although the visible content is Japanese; the site advertises several localized variants.
findings.suggestedFix: Set correct lang on every template and audit logical properties and localized alternates.

findings.summary: The login form obstructs browser autofill.
findings.evidence: Both email and password inputs use autocomplete=off and have no labels, despite being standard sign-in fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=username and current-password, visible labels, and passkey-friendly conditional authentication.

findings.summary: Asset delivery is wasteful for the primarily transactional page.
findings.evidence: The page transfers 5.84MB; image audit found 82 legacy images, 38 without responsive sources, and 30 below-fold images loaded eagerly.
findings.suggestedFix: Convert and right-size imagery, use srcset/sizes, and lazy-load noncritical campaign media.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts consume most transferred bytes before user intent.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 4.56MB of 5.84MB and 276 of 481 requests, dominated by analytics and advertising scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget and defer background measurement and advertising until justified.

findings.summary: Booking capabilities are not exposed as structured agent tools.
findings.evidence: The site has rich search and booking forms but probes found no WebMCP or agent-tool registration, leaving agents to infer legacy form behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose narrowly scoped, confirmable search and booking-assistance tools with clear schemas and user control.

findings.summary: The activity landing page has a large baseline memory footprint.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap snapshot reported 1,052,755 heap nodes and 61.36MB self size; Performance memory reported 69.8MB used JS heap for a landing/search page.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce script/tag populations and release data structures that are not needed for the current task.

taskList.title: Make every core template genuinely responsive and touch-usable
Cut and defer third-party scripts to restore load performance and privacy
Deploy defensive headers and secure cookie attributes
Repair labels, alt text, contrast, headings, and target sizes
Reduce promotional chrome around the core search task
Modernize responsive image and asset delivery
Provide passkeys and standards-based autofill on login
Server-render stable metadata and core content
Add language metadata across legacy localized templates
Expose safe structured agent search capabilities
